chunks: Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd ibn Ḥukaym narrated to me from Salamah ibn Khaťťāb, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Aḥmad, from Bakr ibn Sāliḥ, from ‘Amr ibn Hishām, from one of our companions, from him, who said:

When you go to (the Ziyārah of the grave of) ‘Ali ibn Mūsā Al-Riďā (a.s.), recite (the following): O Allāh! Send Your blessing on ‘Ali ibn Mūsā Al-Riďā, the pleasant, the pious and pure Imam, Your Decisive Proof on those on earth and those under the dust, the truthful, and the martyr. (O Allāh! Send) an increasing, growing, purified, continuous, and a frequent blessing (on him) that is consecutive and greater than any of the blessings You have sent on any of Your friends.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Riḍā (The Pleasing One), a title of Imam ‘Ali ibn Mūsā

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when visiting the grave of Imam Al-Rida?
ai.summary: Compiled by Ibn Qulawayh in *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this supplication emphasizes the Imam’s role as *Hujjat Allah* (God’s Proof) over all creation, reflecting the Shia theological concept of the Imam as the cosmic intermediary. The invocation’s emphasis on continuous and abundant blessings (*salawat*) mirrors the Qur’anic command to send blessings upon the Prophet and his purified household, reinforcing the spiritual connection between the visitor and the Imam’s divine station.
